correctness.rationale: The characteristic abelian ideal V is recovered without assuming it is preserved; the relation BN=aNB produces all invertible automorphisms, with a free translation vector. For multipliers of order r prime to char(F_q), the norm and rth-root argument conjugates any truncated-polynomial unit cocycle to a unique invariant factor; uniformity is proved by surjectivity of the norm. Residue-class decomposition yields the exact kernel-dimension polynomial. Summing group parameters recovers (q−1)²q^(2m−1). Standalone independent exhaustive generator-image tests verify six (q,m) pairs including F_4 and the characteristic-two boundary. The proof, not finite tests, covers every prime-power q and m≥3; m=2 is expressly excluded.

originality.rationale: After comparing full statements and coverage, the exact all-dimension fixed-space polynomial, cyclic-unit reduction and q-1 arithmetic threshold are not present in inspected primary literature or in closest public research records. General structural formulas for almost-abelian automorphisms are prior art and do not themselves tabulate the fixed-space spectrum; a nontrivial new norm-conjugacy and valuation calculation yields its coefficients. Search is not a proof of uniqueness, and older fixed-space or semilinear normal-form literature remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite family of maximal-class nilpotent Lie algebras, a complete automorphism fixed-space spectrum strengthens ordinary group-order calculations and identifies a finite-field arithmetic obstruction to fixed-point-free automorphisms. This has direct relevance to fixed-vector automorphism classifications and gives all nullity moments and probabilities, with a concrete sharp threshold and an unexpected stabilization in dimension. The work is not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the known automorphism form.
